previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG and stents, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, diabetes, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for chest pain that occurred one hour after a dialysis session. The pain was described as squeezing with back radiation and diaphoresis, similar to prior myocardial infarctions, but was unresponsive to sublingual nitroglycerin. Evaluation showed stable troponin levels and EKG changes without diagnostic evolution, indicating angina rather than acute myocardial infarction. The patient was managed with increased isosorbide mononitrate (Imdur) to 120 mg daily, continued beta-blockade, and antiplatelet therapy. He remained chest pain-free, completed hemodialysis without complications, and was discharged home with cardiology follow-up and optimized anti-anginal regimen.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ male with chest pain.

___.

CHEST, PA AND LATERAL:  CABG changes are present, with median sternotomy wires
and mediastinal clips.  Right atrial and ventricular pacemaker courses in
expected position.  Moderate cardiomegaly and small loculated right pleural
effusion persist.  Other than bibasilar atelectasis and some scarring at the
right lung base, the lungs remain clear.  There is no pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION:  Stable findings over multiple examinations.
